stem: Siddharth joins equal-sized nichrome and copper wires, one at a time, to the same cell for the same short time. Both wires carry the same current. The nichrome wire feels warmer than the copper wire.

options.text: Resistance to the current produces heat in each wire; nichrome produces more heat than copper under these conditions.
The nichrome wire must become warm first; its warmth then makes the current flow.
Only nichrome wires become warm when electric current flows.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

part_answers.answer: Current through a conductor meets resistance and produces heat; different materials can produce different amounts of heat for the same current.

teacher.key_rationale: Heating is from resistance to current. Nichrome produces more heat than copper here; warmth does not cause the current, and copper also warms when current flows.
